samples.summary: The report's framing paragraph still ASSERTS, with no input, that no precision figure appears anywhere — and §6 can now print one. `renderWhatThisIsNot()` hardcodes "There is no precision figure, no recall figure and no correctness figure anywhere in this document, because producing one requires adjudicated labels and none exist yet", and the diff only appends a cross-reference to §6 rather than deriving the claim. §6 is precisely the section that renders a present precision cell the moment validity labels exist: this branch's own fixture proves it, since `renderReport(WITH_REVIEWER({ validity: labelledValidity() }))` puts `0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` on the page under the same paragraph claiming no precision figure exists (report.test.mjs ~line 2085). This is the identical defect the same PR family already fixed once for §7's first limit ("No adjudicated labels exist." → derived from the label census, see the task doc's follow-up ③ and `labelsLimit`), so the module's own discipline — a sentence that cannot go red when its premise moves is a falsehood waiting to publish — is violated in the one paragraph the report puts above every number.
samples.evidence: report.mjs:1751-1755 hardcodes the claim; report.test.mjs asserts a present precision cell (`0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)`) is rendered in the same document.

samples.summary: `LENS_COLUMNS` is a hand-written parallel copy of four of `config-hash.mjs`'s eleven `HASHED_LENS_FIELDS`, and its own docblock states the membership rule it then does not apply. `HASHED_LENS_FIELDS` exists precisely so "a field added to `lenses.json` that nobody adds to a hardcoded list" fails a test (config-hash.mjs:89-110); nothing pins `LENS_COLUMNS` against it. Consequences: `needsIssueSpec`, `appliesWhen`, `scopeClasses`, `maxTurns` and `title` all change what a lens does (they are hashed) yet are neither printed on the reviewer table nor part of `lensSignature`, so the cross-replicate "lens set" axis cannot see a leg whose lens differs only in those fields — while the block's stated contract is "if changing it does not change the hash it does not change the reviewer". Deriving the columns from the exported list (minus the two explicitly excluded, `rubric_sha256` for width) would make the table grow with the config instead of drifting behind it.
samples.evidence: report.mjs LENS_COLUMNS (model/samples/effort/gating) vs config-hash.mjs:98-110 HASHED_LENS_FIELDS (11 entries).
searchedFor: grep for an existing lens-table renderer (`| lens |`, `l.model`) across scripts/agent

samples.summary: The `panel code` row conflates two different absences, which is the exact distinction this module is built to keep apart. `panelSha` is null both when the axis DISAGREES and when every envelope simply states no `panel_sha` (`agreed.panel_sha === NOT_STATED`, reachable whenever the report's `--panel-sha` flag supplies the sha for a store whose `run.json`s lack it), yet the row prints "**disagrees across replicates — see below**" in both cases — with no corresponding row in the disagreement table in the second case. A stated-absence ("not stated") is a different fact from a disagreement, and the block's own docblock says a disagreement is reported "never resolved" rather than invented.
samples.evidence: report.mjs `panelSha = agreed.panel_sha && agreed.panel_sha !== NOT_STATED ? … : null` then `d.panel_sha ? … : "| panel code | **disagrees across replicates — see below** |"`.

samples.summary: Section numbers are literals rather than derived from `SECTIONS`, and this change is the demonstration of the cost: adding one section required hand-renumbering "## 6." → "## 7.", plus §6→§7 edits in four docblocks and ~10 test assertions, and the new framing paragraph hardcodes the string "§6". `SECTIONS` is declared to be "the contract" (report.test.mjs) and already carries `key`/`title`, so the index that produces the heading number could come from it; as written the next section addition repeats the same sweep, and any prose reference that is missed points silently at the wrong section.
samples.evidence: renderValidity's heading `"## 6. Is any of it true …"`, renderLimits' `"## 7. Limits …"`, and the diff's §6→§7 comment/test churn; test helper `sectionHeading()` restates the numbers a third time.

samples.summary: `validity-v1` is a string literal in `SECTIONS` while this module pins every other cross-module vocabulary at import (`pin(SCORE_SCOPES…)`, `pin(LABEL_SOURCES…)`, and validity.mjs pins the availability vocabulary in the other direction). Nothing holds this literal against `validity.mjs`'s exported `SCORER_ID`, so a rename there files payloads under a key the renderer never looks for and §6 reads "not computed" over a score sitting in the store — the failure mode the accompanying test comment claims is prevented but only asserts as `SCORER_IDS.includes("validity-v1")`, i.e. against the same literal.
samples.evidence: report.mjs SECTIONS entry `scorer_id: "validity-v1"`; validity.mjs:106 `export const SCORER_ID = "validity-v1"`; report.test.mjs `assert.ok(SCORER_IDS.includes("validity-v1"))`.

samples.summary: Scope: three independently reviewable changes are bundled. Wiring `validity-v1` into the report and the scoring lane is the core of the change; the reviewer-provenance header (`reviewerFigures`, `LENS_COLUMNS`, `renderReviewer`, a new `reviewer_detail` field on the report envelope) and the §1/§3 explanatory prose pass touch neither validity nor each other. The prose pass in particular is a presentation change to two unrelated sections riding along with a metric wiring, which is what makes the numbering/comment churn in this diff hard to separate from behaviour. Declared in the task doc, so this is a packaging preference rather than an unmet requirement.
samples.evidence: renderVolume/renderReliability prose additions and the whole `who the reviewer was` block sit in the same diff as the validity section and `score-all.mjs`'s budget model change.

samples.summary: No design doc records the eval report/scoring subsystem, despite CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 requiring a design doc under `docs/design/` for a non-trivial change (this one adds a report section, a new `reviewer_detail` payload shape on the report envelope, and changes the lane's API-cost model and exit-code contract). The change is documented only as a follow-up section in `docs/tasks/active/20260812-eval-report-renderer-todo.md`. Mitigating: the entire `scripts/agent/eval/` subsystem has no `docs/design/` entry and its sibling merged PRs (validity scorer, report renderer, scoring lane) also used task docs only, so the precedent may be that this area is deliberately task-doc-only.
samples.evidence: docs/design contains no file mentioning scripts/agent/eval, report.mjs, scorers or comparability keys; CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :58-65 state the design-doc-then-task-plan workflow.
searchedFor: grep design doc requirement in CONTRIBUTING.md

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `renderWhatThisIsNot()` (scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs:1747-1762) takes no input and hardcodes "There is no precision figure, no recall figure and no correctness figure anywhere in this document, because producing one requires adjudicated labels and none exist yet"; it is pushed unconditionally from renderReport (report.mjs:1650) above renderValidity (report.mjs:1657). §6's renderValidity does render present precision cells (report.mjs:2654-2658), and the branch's own test renders a FULL report with labelled validity and asserts `0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` appears (report.test.mjs:2050, 2056; fixture at 1895-1913, figure asserted present at 2036). So the identical document can carry both the "no precision figure anywhere" paragraph and a precision figure. The same PR family already applied the derived-claim discipline to the sibling sentence — labelsLimit() is derived from the complementarity label census with an explicit "an assertion with no input … could not go red" rationale (report.mjs:2757-2792), recorded as follow-up ③ in docs/tasks/active/20260812-eval-report-renderer-todo.md:613-617 and 681-689 — and the framing paragraph was left as a bare assertion, receiving only a cross-reference. No guard elsewhere makes the labelled-validity path unreachable, and the code is present exactly as described, so no refutation ground applies.
